title: Renewal + Expansion Check-in - Cobalt Payments
next_steps: Samir to send updated 12-month pricing and committed capacity tiers
Jules to schedule deep-dive benchmark run for APAC latency (week of 2/8)
Customer to confirm regions and signed SOW by 2/18
action_items: Samir: send renewal quote + dedicated capacity options by 2027-02-04
Jules: run perf benchmark (nv12 payloads) and share results by 2027-02-10
Maya: confirm required APAC regions and data residency constraints by 2027-02-11
summary: AE/SE check-in to discuss Cobalt's upcoming renewal, request to expand Dedicated capacity and add APAC regions, and to negotiate a 12-month contract extension. Security/compliance and pricing were reviewed; next steps include sending an updated quote, scheduling performance benchmarks, and finalizing SOW.
transcript: 00:00:03 Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Samir from Redwood - quick roll call?
00:00:10 Maya: Maya here, CTO. Hi Samir, hi Jules.
00:00:14 Devon: Devon, infrastructure lead. Morning.
00:00:18 Lara: Lara from procurement, on mute mostly.
00:00:30 Samir: Great, agenda — quick renewal status, capacity ask (dedicated GPUs), APAC regions, security questions, then next steps. Sound good?
00:01:02 Maya: Yep that's us. We're approaching renewal end of March and we want to lock in more capacity plus add Singapore and Tokyo nodes.
00:01:20 Jules: Got it. Can you share current utilization? that helps size the dedicated pools and autoscale profiles.
00:01:35 Devon: We're at about 70% sustained during peak 9am-1pm ET, bursts to 95%. Token throughput has increased ~30% since last quarter due to new recs flow.
00:02:05 Samir: Okay so increasing committed capacity makes sense. Two questions: target SLA/latency for endpoints, and are you okay with Dedicated in multiple regions or prefer cross-region routing?
00:02:30 Maya: Latency target for customer-facing chat is <250ms 95p. For batch reranks we're ok with higher latency. We prefer regional endpoints — compliance reasons for APAC.
00:03:02 Lara: And procurement will need an addendum for data residency in Singapore; any standard clauses?

00:03:18 Jules: We have a Private/ Dedicated offering with regional isolation and audit logs. I'll share the security pack. Note: sometimes the transcript tool says 'Redwood privet' but it's Redwood Private.
00:03:45 Omar: Quick perf question — our prompt lengths changed. We want to make sure KV cache behaves with multi-shard models, any gotchas?

00:04:05 Jules: KV cache is supported across our runtime, we do continuous batching and KV eviction policies. For multi-shard, kernel selection can re-route, slight jitter might happen during rollouts but we have fallback to smaller quantized variants.
00:04:40 Devon: When you say fallback, is that automatic? we don't want surprises in production during peak.
00:04:55 Jules: It's policy driven — you can opt-in for automatic fallback to pre-approved model variants or fall back to hosted pool. We'll show the rollout policy config in the deep dive.
00:05:30 Samir: On pricing, you mentioned committed spend vs on-demand. We can propose a tiered commit for 12 months with burst credits. Maya, is 12 months your preferred term?
00:05:50 Maya: Yes, 12 months is preferred. Could be 24 if pricing delta is material but start with 12.
00:06:10 Lara: We'll need a fixed commit line item for budget planning; can you provide examples of committed tiers matched to observed throughput?
00:06:30 Samir: We'll send a model — e.g., small/medium/large pools with expected rps and token rates plus estimated monthly cost and overage policy.
00:07:05 Maya: Also want additional regions: Singapore and Tokyo as I said, and possibly Sydney later. Any extra setup time for APAC?
00:07:22 Jules: For Dedicated we can provision region pools; lead time usually 2-3 weeks for capacity allocation, plus network peering setup if you want VPC peering.
00:07:45 Devon: For VPC peering we'll need details — route tables, CIDR, and also SAML SSO integration with Okta. Is Okta SAML standard?
00:08:00 Samir: Yes Okta SAML is standard; we support SAML 2.0 and SCIM for provisioning. We'll include the SSO setup guide in the security package link.
00:08:25 Maya: Good. On audits — do you have SOC 2 type II? we need to present that to our compliance team.
00:08:35 Jules: We have SOC 2 and ISO certs; I'll paste the SOC 2 cert and the pen test summary in the follow-up. There's also an SOC 2 addendum for dedicated environments.
00:09:02 Lara: Excellent. Procurement will want redlines. Are there any non-standard legal terms for dedicated?
00:09:15 Samir: Typically we add committed capacity and SLA terms; nothing wildly different. We'll flag the SOW and the data residency appendix for your legal team.
00:09:40 Omar: On the tech side, can we run a smoke benchmark before commit? we want end-to-end latency from APAC clients to the Singapore pool.
00:09:55 Jules: Yes — planned deep-dive benchmark. We'll do end-to-end tests: cold start, warm KV cache, and simulated burst. Expect to capture p50/p95/p99 and token throughput.
00:10:25 Devon: How long does the benchmark take? we have limited windows for infra tests.
00:10:33 Jules: Benchmarks typically run 2-4 hours including warm-up. We'll coordinate a window. I can run one in our staging APAC nodes next Tuesday.
00:11:00 Maya: Perfect. One more security question — key management. We want our keys in our KMS. Do you support customer-managed keys?
00:11:10 Samir: Yes, we support KMS/HSM integrations for Dedicated and Private. We'll share KMS integration steps and required IAM roles.
00:11:35 Lara: On billing, we'll need invoices aligned to commit months; can you do monthly invoices tied to committed units?
00:11:45 Samir: Yes, monthly invoicing is standard. We'll have a committed-unit line and an overage line for bursts.
00:12:05 Maya: Any known limits for quantized models in Dedicated? we've seen some artifacts with 4-bit quant on other platforms.

00:12:18 Jules: Quantization profiles vary by model. We'll recommend specific quant profiles per model; there is sometimes small quality degradation — we'll include regen tests in the benchmark and the Optimize recommendations.
00:12:50 Devon: Can we get a runbook for failover — if Singapore pool drops, automatic route to Tokyo? We want predictable failover and no traffic blackhole.
00:13:02 Jules: Yes, smart routing policies allow region preference and cross-region fallback. We can pre-approve fallback model variants to control cost/latency tradeoffs.
00:13:30 Maya: Okay real quick — decision owners: I'll be final approver on architecture, Lara will sign contracts, Devon will sign off on infra tests. Timeline to lock by mid-February?
00:13:45 Lara: That's tight but doable if quotes land this week.
00:13:55 Samir: We'll aim to send updated quote by Thursday 2/4. We'll include committed tiers, latency SLAs, and a SOW draft for APAC addendum.
00:14:20 Omar: A couple of minor items — can we get a sample config for autoscale policy? we want to mimic current burst patterns.
00:14:30 Jules: I'll attach example autoscale JSON and recommended thresholds. Note sometimes the transcript mislabels 'KV cache' as 'K V cash' so just a heads up, the doc will be clear.
00:15:05 Maya: Sounds good. Anything else on the roadmap we should know about?
00:15:12 Samir: We're rolling out improved batching heuristics and a new Optimize dashboard that shows per-route cost and quality tradeoffs; expect beta in Q2.
00:15:35 Devon: Will that give per-token cost breakouts?
00:15:40 Samir: Yes — token-level cost and latencies plus recommendations for quantization and batching.
00:16:00 Maya: Great. Let's recap next steps.

00:16:10 Samir: Recap: Samir send quote + SOW draft by 2/4; Jules schedule benchmark and run by 2/10 and share results; Maya confirm APAC regions by 2/11; Lara start procurement paperwork on receipt of quote.
00:16:40 Lara: We'll aim to have PO ready once quote aligns to budget.
00:16:50 Samir: Any blockers on our side?
00:17:00 Maya: Not right now. The compliance team might ask for extra details but we usually clear that quickly.
00:17:12 Samir: Perfect. We'll follow up with three artifacts: quote/SOW, security pack link, benchmark schedule. Links: /links/quote-cobalt-2027, /links/security-pack, /links/benchmark-sheet.
00:17:35 Omar: Thanks everyone. Appreciate the clarity on fallback policies.
00:17:40 Samir: Thanks all — we'll send notes and action items. Bye.
00:17:45 Maya: Bye.
00:17:48 Devon: Bye.
00:17:50 Lara: Thanks, bye.
00:18:05 (call ended)
